name: Lviv Town Hall
elevationDatum: Rigid local foundation y=0; real metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Two mapped controls fix rotation, baked into the geometry once. No terrain or Mercator stretch.
note: Lviv’s four-wing neoclassical town hall encloses the mapped open courtyard beneath low metal hip roofs; its set-back three-tier 65 m clock tower has a broad observation balcony and toothed roof crown. The 65 m tower height is published by Lviv tourism; rooftop flagpole is omitted so the structural height is explicit. OSM main-body height 15 m appears too low for the photographed four-storey facade; 22.7 m eaves and 26.2 m ridge are original estimates, not a survey. Clock/upper-tier widths, roof pitch, balcony and portico are photo estimates. The pre-1826 illustration and plaque-only photograph are excluded as current exterior references. Upper part 589215113 is a different tower roughly 130 m away and is not owned. Cityscape: not tested; Full 3D world: not tested. Review follow-up: Far window frames are simplified into individual rectangular panes with wider bay grouping, preserving four window rows, the central arched group, courtyard void, clocks, gallery rail and toothed crown.
